title: Tool-Gated Residual Distillation for DataChef Verifier Scoring

contributions.purpose: Show that LLM rubric verifier scores fail to predict downstream fine-tuned model quality in data curation.
contributions.mechanism: Correlate teacher LLM rubric scores of candidate datasets against downstream benchmark performance of models fine-tuned on those datasets, across two held-out DataChef tasks (LiveCodeBench, OpenFinData).
contributions.evaluation: LLM-only verifier scores anti-correlate with downstream performance (average Spearman rho = -0.405), meaning higher-rated datasets tend to produce worse fine-tuned models.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that LLM rubric scores anti-correlate with downstream performance (rho = -0.405), challenging assumptions in rubric-based data curation.

contributions.purpose: Provide a lightweight verifier that better predicts which datasets yield stronger fine-tuned models.
contributions.mechanism: Tool-Gated Residual Distillation factorizes verification: deterministic tool gating handles structural failures (empty responses, repetition) while a small distilled Qwen2.5-1.5B LoRA student learns a 3-way semantic classification from teacher labels.
contributions.evaluation: Tool+Distilled achieves average Spearman rho = 0.771 with downstream benchmark scores (a 1.18-point improvement over the -0.405 LLM-only baseline) and zero top-1 regret, always selecting the ground-truth best dataset.
contributions.source_quote: We propose tool-gated residual distillation, achieving rho = 0.771 correlation and zero top-1 regret (always selecting the ground-truth best dataset).

contributions.purpose: Eliminate the inference-time cost of teacher LLM verification.
contributions.mechanism: Replace per-instance teacher API scoring with the distilled student plus deterministic tool gates so no teacher calls are needed at inference.
contributions.evaluation: Reduces inference cost from 2.56M teacher tokens to zero API calls while improving ranking fidelity.
contributions.source_quote: We eliminate inference-time teacher API calls, reducing cost from 2.56M tokens to zero while improving ranking fidelity.

self_declared_provenance.quote: However, a critical limitation of LLM-as-a-judge approaches is their computational cost and the assumption that rubric-based quality assessments correlate with downstream task performance—an assumption we empirically challenge in this work.
Our work addresses this limitation by distilling the verifier into a lightweight model that eliminates inference-time costs while improving correlation with downstream performance.

Our approach combines these threads by using deterministic tool gating to handle structural failures while distilling a small LoRA-adapted student model for semantic classification, achieving both efficiency and improved downstream correlation.

notes: Central claim rests on a surprising anti-correlation finding for the teacher LLM verifier (rho = -0.405): the distilled student outperforming its own teacher is the paper's headline anomaly ('despite significant divergence from teacher predictions'). Evaluation limited to two held-out DataChef tasks.
